(8.) Solid Waste Disposal
The City disposes of its solid waste by incineration and sanitary landfill. The new incinerator, presently undergoing final testing to determine if it meets Federal and State air quality standards (May, 1973), has a capacity of 800 tons per day (TPD). At present it is processing approximately 120 TPD for the City of Harrisburg. The plant will also service the solid waste needs for other surrounding jurisdictions.
Solid waste collection is accomplished by the City with its own equipment. The project area is serviced once a week. In some areas of the project it was observed that littering, apparently from overturned trash cans between collection periods, is a problem.
(9.) Social Resources and Related Services
A wide range of non-profit and governmental agencies are located in Harrisburg to provide the residents of the project, the City and, the surrounding jurisdictions, with social services in the areas of financial and employment assistance, community wide services, family and children services, health services, and recreational services. A partial list of these agencies follow (agencies that are known to be located within the project area or immediately adjacent to the project area are indicated by an asterisk; those known to be directly serving the project area are underscored):
a. Agencies of Financial and Employment Assistance:
The Bethesda Mission.
B'nai B'rith Vocational Service.
